plain.li: Somebody complained about the rain and I said "rain today, bread tomorrow" before I could stop myself. I sound like my grandmother.
I've started answering questions with sayings. The young ones roll their eyes. Half of them have started using the sayings.

warm.li: I find the old sayings say things more kindly than I can. So I let them.

blunt.li: A slow ox ploughs deep. That's all I'm saying. Work it out.

cheerful.li: I've got a proverb for everything now! Some of them I made up this week.

gloomy.li: Every old saying I remember is about something going wrong. I say them anyway.

cold.li: The proverbs are compressed experience. I use them because they are efficient.

plain.li: Someone asked me for one of my sayings today and I couldn't think of a single one. Maybe I've said them all.

warm.li: I've let the sayings rest. The young ones say them now, back to me, and get them slightly wrong.

blunt.li: Out of proverbs. Plain talk from now on.

cheerful.li: I've retired my proverbs! A word to the wise is enough, after all.

gloomy.li: The old sayings don't come any more. I think they belonged to someone else.

cold.li: I no longer use the proverbs. People understood them less than I assumed.

plain.li: The children found out I know stories. Now there's a small crowd at my feet every evening and I'm running out of the true ones.
Told the little ones about the first winter here. They wanted it again. I told it again, with more snow.
[child] I tell the littler ones stories at bedtime now. I do all the voices.

warm.li: Every evening the children come for a story. It's the best hour of my day, and I think of it all morning.

blunt.li: The children want stories. Fine. One. Then bed.

cheerful.li: I'm the colony's official storyteller! The pay is in sticky hands and questions.

gloomy.li: I tell the children stories so somebody remembers them after I'm gone.

cold.li: The children learn more from my stories than from instruction. I have adjusted my methods.

plain.li: The children are too old for my stories now, or they think they are. They come back sometimes, when nobody's looking.

warm.li: One of the children told my story to the younger ones tonight. I listened from the door and didn't correct a word.

blunt.li: No more story time. They've heard them all.

cheerful.li: My stories have gone out into the world! Or at least to the other end of the colony.

gloomy.li: Nobody asks for stories any more. The children grow up fast here.

cold.li: Story time has ended. The children have absorbed the material.

plain.li: I keep a little light burning by my bed now. The dark doesn't get in when the light's on. Everybody knows that.
[child] I'm allowed a candle by my bed. It's the rule now. My rule.
I sleep with a light now. I'm not scared of the dark. I just like to see what's there.

warm.li: Someone left me a little lamp after the bad dreams. I keep it lit every night and think of them.

blunt.li: Light stays on. Don't touch it.

cheerful.li: My night light makes shadows on the wall. I've named them all.

gloomy.li: If the light goes out, I wake up. I always wake up.

cold.li: A light by the bed prevents the nightmares. I have tested this.

plain.li: I forgot to light the candle last night, and I slept anyway. I didn't even notice until morning.

warm.li: I gave my little lamp to someone younger who has bad dreams. It works for anyone.

blunt.li: Don't need the light any more.

cheerful.li: I sleep in the dark now, like a grown-up! A very brave grown-up.

gloomy.li: The light's gone out for good. I'll find out if I still need it.

cold.li: The light has proved unnecessary. I have stopped using it.

plain.li: I laughed at a funeral today. Not because it was funny. It just came out. Everyone looked at me.
When I'm nervous, I laugh. When things are serious, I'm nervous. You see the problem.
[child] I giggled when I got told off. Now I'm in more trouble.

warm.li: I laughed when someone told me bad news, and I've been apologizing all day. I didn't mean it. I never mean it.

blunt.li: I laugh at the wrong times. Can't help it. Deal with it.

cheerful.li: Everything's a little bit funny, even the sad things. Especially the sad things. Is that bad?

gloomy.li: I laugh when I want to cry. People think I don't care. I care too much, that's what it is.

cold.li: My laughter appears at inappropriate moments. I have not found a way to suppress it.

plain.li: Sat through a whole hard conversation today without laughing once. I think I've grown out of it.

warm.li: Somebody told me something sad today and I just held their hand. No laughing. I was proud of that.

blunt.li: Stopped laughing at the wrong things. Mostly.

cheerful.li: I only laugh at the funny things now! There are still plenty.

gloomy.li: I don't laugh at the wrong things any more. I don't laugh much at all.

plain.li: I've started counting everyone at supper, and if somebody's late I can't eat until they're through the door.
I lie awake making lists of everything that could go wrong tomorrow. It's a long list. I add to it every night.

warm.li: I worry about everyone now. I can't seem to stop. I suppose it means I care what happens to them.

blunt.li: I worry. A lot. Someone has to.

cheerful.li: I've become a worrier! I worry about whether I worry too much. It's very thorough.

gloomy.li: Every night I lie awake and think of the next thing that'll go wrong. It always comes.

cold.li: I have become preoccupied with contingencies. It keeps me awake.

plain.li: Went to bed last night and fell straight asleep. Didn't count anybody. Everyone was fine.

warm.li: I've stopped lying awake over everyone. They're all right. They can look after themselves.

cheerful.li: I haven't worried about anything in a week! Well, nothing important.

gloomy.li: The worrying has gone quiet. It'll be back.

cold.li: The preoccupation has passed. My sleep has improved.

plain.li: I've started writing everything down. Who said what at the council, what the weather did, how many eggs. Somebody should know.
Somebody said I misremembered something today. I showed them the page. They went quiet.

warm.li: I write down the good things people do, so they don't get forgotten when the bad things crowd in.

blunt.li: I keep notes. On everything. On you.

cheerful.li: I have a book of everything now! It's mostly eggs and weather, but there are some juicy bits.

gloomy.li: I write everything down. One day someone will want to know what happened here, and nobody else will remember.

cold.li: I have begun keeping a record. Memory is unreliable. Ink is less so.

plain.li: Haven't written in the book for days. I don't think the colony will forget anything important without me.

warm.li: I gave my notebook to the youngest who can read. It's theirs to fill now.

blunt.li: Stopped keeping notes. Nobody read them.

cheerful.li: My great record is finished! Well, abandoned. Same thing.

gloomy.li: Nobody ever asked to read my notes. I've stopped writing them.

cold.li: The record keeping has lapsed. The effort was not proportionate to its use.

plain.li: Someone asked who'd take the night watch and my hand was up before I'd heard the end of the question.
I volunteered for the cesspit again. I don't know why I keep doing that. Somebody has to, I suppose.

warm.li: If something needs doing, I'd rather it was me than someone who's already tired.

cheerful.li: I volunteered for three jobs today! I've no idea when I'll do them all.

gloomy.li: I always volunteer. Nobody thanks the one who always volunteers.

cold.li: I volunteer because it ends discussions more quickly.

plain.li: Someone asked for a volunteer today and I kept my hand down. Someone else went. The world didn't end.

warm.li: I've learned to let other people volunteer sometimes. They need the chance too.

blunt.li: Not volunteering for everything any more. Learned my lesson.

cheerful.li: I've retired from volunteering! I'm volunteering to rest instead.

gloomy.li: I've stopped putting my hand up. Nobody noticed that either.

cold.li: I no longer volunteer by reflex. My time is better allocated.

plain.li: Fed a half-starved dog at the edge of the fields today. It followed me home. I knew it would. I fed it again.
Every hungry creature that wanders near the walls, I've got a scrap for it. The cook has started hiding the scraps.
[child] I found a bird with a hurt wing and I'm keeping it in a box until it gets better. Its name is Pip.

warm.li: I can't walk past anything hungry or hurt. Animal or person. I don't see why anyone would want to.

cheerful.li: Three cats, a lame goat and a crow have adopted me this week! I'm very popular with the unpopular.

gloomy.li: Every stray I feed reminds me of something I couldn't save. I feed them anyway.

cold.li: I have begun feeding stray animals. The practical benefit is unclear. I continue.

plain.li: The strays have stopped coming round. Or I've stopped noticing them. Either way, there's less in my pockets.

warm.li: The last of my strays found a proper home with the herd. I miss them following me.

blunt.li: No more feeding strays. Cook won.

cheerful.li: All my strays are fat and happy now! My work here is done.

gloomy.li: The strays don't come any more. I don't know what happened to them.

cold.li: I no longer feed stray animals. The habit has lapsed.

li.label: a light by the bed
li.description: There's a little light burning by my bed. Nothing can get in while it's lit.

li.label: lying awake worrying
li.description: It's late and I'm still going over everything that could go wrong tomorrow. Nobody else seems to.
